original_test_intent: Validate uncorrectable xGMI3 handling for each required inter-socket direction or endpoint, with attributable reporting, project-defined containment/reset behavior and verified peer/fabric recovery.
original_method: Build an owner-approved link/direction/socket/errorlocation map from tool enumeration and package documentation; capture platform/BIOS/HDT/tool/OS baseline; resolve UCE labels and expected disposition; execute at most one mapped UCE under continuous OOB observation; preserve tool, MCA/APEI or WHEA, BMC/UEFI, console and both-peer link evidence; fully recover and review before any separately approved second direction; restore state.
manual_activity: A qualified FAE resolves selector and UCE semantics, provisions the licensed injector/HDT, supervises one mapped fabric UCE and OOB recovery, explicitly authorizes any second direction, then restores BIOS/HDT state.
required_inputs: Multi-socket xGMI physical topology and tool link/direction/source/destination map
Decision whether errorlocation 0/1 selects Socket 1/0, IOD/CCD or another endpoint
Confirmation that errortype 1 is UCE despite Correctable step labels
AMD tool/spec version/hash/license and linktraffic semantics
Expected per-direction UCE severity, sync-flood/reset/crash/containment, console and recovery timeout
Linux MCA/APEI/dmesg versus Windows WHEA plus peer counters and BMC/UEFI oracle
BIOS FFE deviation, backup, hard abort, OOB recovery and restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated non-production multi-socket SUT with data protection and independent OOB console/power/reimage path
Do not substitute the placeholder or inject until selector/severity/disposition are authoritative
One UCE on one mapped direction only; require complete recovery and new approval before another
Abort on wrong endpoint, severity escalation beyond plan, error storm, unexpected reset, peer loss, degraded link or lost console
No automatic retry/recovery; close injector and restore/diff all settings
agent_execution_scope: Validate approved topology, package provenance, UCE oracle, abort and recovery readiness
Collect read-only tool, OS, BMC/UEFI, console, peer counters and post-recovery integrity evidence
Do not infer selectors, change BIOS/HDT, inject, authorize a second checkpoint, reset/reimage/retry or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Resolve Correctable labels and socket-versus-errorlocation semantics
Approve exact link/direction, UCE disposition and one-shot command
Own OOB recovery and separately authorize any second direction

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic xGMI log filtering cannot prove direction, endpoint or whether a reset/crash was expected containment rather than uncontrolled damage.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Replace the placeholder only from an approved topology map and execute one errortype-1 command on one direction under OOB monitoring; do not chain the peer command.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Two socket-labeled checkpoints, errorlocation 0/1, linktraffic 1, errortype 1, BIOS controls and 30/20-minute estimate are preserved pending semantic resolution.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat each xGMI UCE direction as an independent destructive checkpoint with exact selector mapping, predicted containment and verified two-peer recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds label resolution, direction/endpoint attribution, continuous console, peer evidence, serialized approval, hard timeouts and rollback.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Two placeholder commands do not prove two sockets, and tool PASS does not prove correct UCE containment or recovered coherent fabric.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An incorrectly targeted xGMI UCE can reset or isolate a socket, corrupt workload state, lose management reachability or leave degraded fabric.

project_override_considerations: If the tool revision documents errorlocation as the remote socket selector, cite it. Otherwise correct the execution package without rewriting Master, retaining the stated Socket 1/0 Coverage and recording the source conflict.
expected_evidence: Exact identity plus approved multi-socket topology/selector map
Tool/spec provenance and BIOS/HDT before/target/restored state
One direction's complete command and continuous OOB console transcript
Attributed UCE MCA/APEI or WHEA, BMC/UEFI and both-peer xGMI counter/link evidence
Expected versus observed containment and bounded recovery/integrity record
Separate authorization for any second direction and engineer verdict

The steps also label errorlocation 0/1 as Socket 1/0 although adjacent rows call them IOD/CCD, retain an unsubstituted link placeholder, omit timeout/containment, and require dmesg for a Windows option.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 41 Wistron-System RAS-00761-V003: confirm errortype=1 UCE despite both steps saying Correctable; approve xGMI link/direction/source/destination topology and whether errorlocation 0/1 means Socket 1/0, IOD/CCD or another endpoint; provide AMD tool/spec version/hash/license, expected sync-flood/reset/crash containment and timeouts, Linux/Windows plus peer/BMC evidence, BIOS deviation, serialized approval, OOB recovery and restoration.

review_improvement: Turns ambiguous placeholder UCE commands into independent direction-specific destructive checkpoints with authoritative semantics, continuous recovery evidence and no automatic chaining.
independent_technical_reasoning: An xGMI UCE affects coherent communication between sockets, so both peers and the selected direction matter. A copied Correctable label and unresolved errorlocation field can cause the wrong destructive stimulus. Tool PASS only proves request handling; expected containment may include reset or isolation and must be distinguished from uncontrolled failure by console and peer evidence. The second direction is a new hazardous action after recovery, not an automatic continuation.
